message.content:
Sure! Here are a few highly recommended Chinese restaurants in New York City across different neighborhoods and price ranges:

| Neighborhood | Restaurant | Highlights | Price Range |
|--------------|------------|------------|-------------|
| **Chinatown (Manhattan)** | **Jing Fong** | Classic dim‑sum, bustling atmosphere, great for large groups. | $10–$25 per person |
| | **Nom Wah Tea Parlor** | Historic spot, excellent egg tarts & traditional dim‑sum. | $8–$20 per person |
| **Upper East Side** | **Ming’s** | Upscale Cantonese cuisine, elegant setting, known for Peking duck. | $30–$60 per person |
| **Brooklyn (Williamsburg)** | **Sushi Nakazawa** (Japanese but offers some Chinese-inspired dishes) | Innovative sushi & small plates, Michelin-starred. | $50–$80 per person |
| | **Lao Sze Chuan** | Authentic Sichuan flavors, spicy hot pot & dry‑fry dishes. | $15–$35 per person |
| **Midtown West** | **Hwa Yuan** | Modern take on classic Cantonese dishes, stylish interior. | $25–$45 per person |
| **Harlem** | **Red Hook** | Contemporary Asian fusion with a focus on sustainable sourcing. | $20–$40 per person |

If you have a specific area or style in mind (e.g., dim‑sum, hot pot, upscale dining), let me know and I can narrow it down further!
